headline: 🔥 **TWO BUYER PARTIES ARE LIVE ON 225 WILLOW POINT AT THE SAME TIME, AND ONE OF THEM IS WRITING AN OFFER THIS MORNING.** Molly G. told you at 6:17 last night her buyers want to make an offer and asked whether you had any others; then at 5:51 this morning Angela W. — the third brokerage through the door — wrote back unprompted that it is “an adorable townhouse” and her buyer is sending the listing to a husband who works out of town. ⭐ FIVE TOURS, THREE BROKERAGES, SEVEN DAYS, AND NOT ONE AGENT HAS ARGUED $185,000. 🎯 The outreach to Angela is sent; the call to ask when the husband can walk it is yours. ⚠️ And two free levers are still unpulled — your sellers' written answer has never reached Molly, and the reply to Anna C. is still sitting unsent in your drafts.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 A THIRD AGENT CAME BACK ON HER OWN AT 5:51 THIS MORNING. Angela W. of ARC Realty 280 — whose buyer arrived late to last night's 6:45 tour — wrote without being chased: “It is an adorable townhouse. Her husband works out of town and she will send the listing to him.” ⭐ A BUYER FORWARDING A HOUSE TO THE PERSON WHO HAS TO AGREE IS THE MOST COMMON SHAPE A SECOND SHOWING TAKES, and it lands on the same morning a different agent delivers an offer.
hotSignals.action: ✅ Agent outreach SENT 7:5x AM — what would it take to get her client in, with closing-cost help, timing and possession flexibility, and a second showing any time for the husband, no price named. 📞 NOW CALL HER: one question — does the husband want to see it, and when? A second walk-through this week with the decision-maker present is worth more than anything else on this listing. ⚠️ The outreach deliberately does NOT mention the inbound offer; if you want the competition said out loud, say it by voice.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 THE OFFER ITSELF. Molly G. of Keller Williams Hoover texted at 6:17 PM: “Buyers want to make an offer. I probably won't be able to get it to you until morning… Do you have any offers yet?” ⭐ SHE TOOK THE FIRST SHOWING THIS LISTING EVER HAD ON 8/21 and came back three days later with buyers who “really liked it.” 🎯 She never argued the price — her only two reservations were a living-room ceiling mark and an unpatched closet.
hotSignals.action: 📞 It lands this morning. ⚠️ THE FREE LEVER IS STILL UNPULLED: your sellers answered both her concerns in writing inside an hour on 8/24 and that answer has never reached her. Send it before you read the offer — it costs nothing and it removes her only two objections.

hotSignals.signal: 🎉 THE FIRST FEEDBACK THIS ADDRESS EVER PRODUCED, and the headline was what she didn't say. Anna C. of A Squared Properties replied twenty minutes after you asked: buyers “really liked it,” it “showed very well,” “you can tell they definitely put in the work” — and when asked directly how $185,000 read, she did not argue the number at all. ⭐ THREE CONCERNS, ALL COSMETIC BY HER OWN READ: a settled Sheetrock joint, whether crown molding is going back, and a patched laundry-room ceiling opening she assumes is an access panel.
hotSignals.action: 📝 YOUR REPLY TO HER IS STILL SITTING UNSENT IN DRAFTS, second morning running. Two of her three questions have answers only your sellers can give and both are almost certainly reassuring. Send it today — with an offer landing, a second agreeable buyer is leverage, not clutter.

hotSignals.signal: 🎉 IT CONVERTED, AND OVERNIGHT IT GOT REAL. The showings stopped mattering when the seller and the buyers agreed Sunday evening at $439,000; the executed seller copy came back at 11:42 last night and your coordinator has asked the buyer's agent to return it once the buyers initial the changes.
hotSignals.action: 🔍 Chase the buyers' initials — initials on changed terms are the last place this can wobble. ⚠️ The underlying risk is unchanged: these buyers must close their own house first, so this is a contingency, not a closing.

hotSignals.signal: 🎯 A FIFTH SHOWING SATURDAY AT 3:00 PM from an agent who had never shown this house before — and separately, a named buyer texted you direct that he would go well under $550,000 and asked outright whether there is room, plus offered you the representation.
hotSignals.action: 📞 He is on today's call list and he is the only person who followed the complaint with an offer to act. 🔍 Saturday's read is now three days outstanding on an address that returns forms about half the time — chase it or write it off. ⭐ The lever that is not a price cut: a pre-inspection, because four agents in a row have said the same thing and unknowns is what a pre-inspection removes.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 THE ONLY UNQUALIFIED YES ON THIS BOARD, AND IT IS NOW DAY TEN. Amy G. of Ethos International filed it herself: interested YES, her buyers just started looking, they really like it, and it sits at the TOP of their list. She phoned from inside the house mid-showing. ⭐ SHE LEFT PRICED-RIGHT BLANK — the objection is unasked, not absent.
hotSignals.action: 📞 Human call, not machine mail — ten days is well past the window where an automated outreach reads right. 🔴 And the basement lights she reported still have no answer; your seller is the only person who knows why.

listings.status: 🔥 ACTIVE — OFFER INBOUND THIS MORNING, day 7

feedback.note: 🔥 UNPROMPTED AT 5:51 AM, REPLYING TO YOUR 7:15 PM ASK: “It is an adorable townhouse. Her husband works out of town and she will send the listing to him.” ⭐ THE TOUR RAN SHORT ONLY BECAUSE HER BUYER ARRIVED LATE — she said so herself at 7:09 PM — so nothing about the house failed; the read simply never got collected on site. 🎯 A buyer forwarding a listing to an out-of-town decision-maker is a second showing waiting to be booked. ✅ Agent outreach sent 7:5x AM.

🔥 “My buyers are interested in 225 Willow Point Cir. They actually really liked it” at 10:27 AM — then at 6:17 PM: “Buyers want to make an offer… I probably won't be able to get it to you until morning. Do you have any offers yet?” ⭐ SHE TOOK THE FIRST SHOWING THIS LISTING EVER HAD. Her only two reservations are a living-room ceiling mark and an unpatched closet, and she asked directly whether the sellers had corrected them. 🎯 She never raised the price. ⚠️ The sellers answered both in writing within the hour and that answer has still not reached her.

🎉 THE FIRST FEEDBACK THIS ADDRESS EVER PRODUCED, twenty minutes after you asked — by email, not through the showing system, which has never once issued a request here. ⭐ THE HEADLINE IS WHAT SHE DIDN'T SAY: asked directly how $185,000 read against everything her buyers have seen, she did not argue the number at all. 🔍 HER WORDS: the buyers “really liked it,” it “showed very well,” and “you can tell they definitely put in the work.” ⚠️ THREE CONCERNS, ALL COSMETIC BY HER OWN READ: a crack she thinks is a settled Sheetrock joint, whether crown molding is going back or being cut in with paint, and a patched laundry-room ceiling opening she assumes is a deliberate access panel.

gaps: Sat 8/22 9:00 AM — held, no feedback returned and no request ever issued on this address
listings.note: 🔥 DAY SEVEN AND IT PEAKED THIS MORNING. Five tours since Friday across three separate brokerages, two live buyer parties at once, an offer being written, and not one agent has argued $185,000. 🎉 THE FEEDBACK DROUGHT THAT LASTED THIS LISTING'S ENTIRE LIFE BROKE THREE TIMES IN 20 HOURS and every verdict was the same: buyers really liked it, concerns purely cosmetic, price not challenged. ⭐ YOUR SELLERS ARE OUTWORKING THE MARKET — they answered both buyer concerns in writing inside an hour, told you they will take showings any time weekday or weekend, renewed the ad spend, and Darrell is cutting in the living-room trim himself. The flood-insurance question has an answer now off their own escrow statement. ⚠️ TWO FREE LEVERS ARE STILL UNPULLED: the sellers' written answer never reached Molly, and the reply to Anna is still unsent. 📅 The ad that found every one of these buyers dies tomorrow.

gaps: Tue 8/11 2:15 PM — held, no feedback ever returned
Fri 8/14 10:30 AM — the second showing that became the offer; no form ever filed
listings.note: ✅ THE SIGNATURE THIS BOARD CALLED MISSING ALL DAY MONDAY CAME BACK AT 11:42 LAST NIGHT. Agreed Sunday at $439,000 with concessions, two and a half per side, and a close date the buyer named; your coordinator has the executed seller copy and has asked the buyer's agent to return it once the buyers initial the changes. ⭐ THAT MOVES IT FROM A HANDSHAKE TO A PAPER DEAL. ⚠️ It is not fully executed until those initials come back. 🔍 Both feedback gaps here are now moot — the second showing turned into the contract, which is the only feedback that ever mattered.

listings.status: ⚠️ ACTIVE — Saturday's read three days outstanding

feedback.note: ❄️ INTERESTED NO, PRICED RIGHT = TOO HIGH, and the worst staging score anything on this board has taken — 1 out of 5. ⭐ THE USEFUL PART IS THE LEVER SHE HANDED YOU AND IT IS NOT A PRICE CUT: her write-up points at unknowns, and a pre-inspection is exactly what removes unknowns on a house institutional sellers will not repair.

❄️ INTERESTED NO, TOO HIGH — the same verdict, filed independently three days earlier. 🔍 FOUR AGENTS IN A ROW HAVE NOW SAID THE IDENTICAL THING about this address, which stops being an opinion and starts being a market reading.

listings.note: 🔍 THIS ADDRESS RETURNS FORMS ABOUT HALF THE TIME, and Saturday's is now three days late. ⚠️ FOUR INDEPENDENT PASSES ON THE SAME GROUND — too high — is not noise. 🎯 THE ONE LIVE THING IS A NAMED BUYER WHO TEXTED GENE DIRECT: he would go well under the ask, asked outright if there is room, and offered Gene the representation. He is on today's call list. ⭐ A weekly report to the asset manager is drafted and waiting to be sent.

She phoned from inside the house mid-showing, so a call back is returned, not cold. ⭐ SHE LEFT PRICED RIGHT BLANK — the objection is unasked, not absent, and only a person can ask it. 🔴 She also reported the basement lights, and that still has no answer from the seller.

❄️ INTERESTED NO — the stairs. Both price fields left blank, so this is a floor-plan pass rather than a price pass. 🔍 Worth remembering when the price conversation eventually comes: this buyer was never going to be a price buyer.

✅ INTERESTED YES AND PRICED JUST RIGHT — the earlier of the two yeses on this address and the only agent who affirmatively endorsed $295,000 in writing. 🔍 Nothing came of it, but it is the second independent voice saying the number is not the problem.

listings.note: 🔥 TWO SEPARATE AGENTS SAID YES ON THIS HOUSE AND NEITHER HAS BEEN CONVERTED. ⚠️ The strongest of the two is now ten days old, which is well past the window where an automated outreach reads right — this is a human call. 🔴 THE ONE OPEN ITEM IS THE SELLER'S, NOT THE MARKET'S: the basement lights were reported by a buyer who liked the house, and nobody has answered it in ten days.

listings.note: ⚠️ THE PRICE CHANGED AND THE INTERNET STILL HAS NOT. The corrected post was rebuilt with seven verified assets and deliberately left as a DRAFT rather than auto-published — your own rule says a price post does not go out unattended — and it is still sitting there this morning. 🔍 No tour has been booked here inside the two-week window at all, which is the number that should be driving the conversation, not the price.

feedback.note: ❄️ INTERESTED NO, but PRICED JUST RIGHT — a showing taken while the unit was already contingent. 🔍 The price endorsement is the useful half: if the contract wobbles, the number is not what would need to change.

listings.note: 🎉 TWO OF THE THREE OPEN ITEMS CLOSED YESTERDAY AFTERNOON — the wire-versus-check question is answered and the home warranty is ordered, invoice and confirmation both in hand. 🔴 THE SURVEY AND THE SEPTIC-AND-SEWER INSPECTION ARE STILL UNANSWERED, asked in writing 8/20, now five days out with the table three days away. ⭐ SEPTIC IS THE ONE THAT CARRIES LEAD TIME — a problem found Thursday does not close Friday. 🎣 A fake title company emailed wire instructions on this file; confirm every wire by voice on a number you already had.

listings.note: 🎉 THE LOOP OPENED AND CLOSED INSIDE ONE BUSINESS DAY. Scope agreed, any licensed roofer acceptable, the buyer's agent said “all good,” and both sellers have now signed. 🔍 Only the escrow holdback sizing remains, and that is a number to agree rather than a condition to fix.

🔴 THE MOST EXPENSIVE LISTING ON THE BOARD AND NOT ONE TOUR HAS EVER BEEN BOOKED ON IT. ⭐ THIS WEEK SHARPENS THE POINT: a $185,000 listing took five tours and an offer in seven days off the same machine that has never produced a single booking here. 🔍 The comp work says the big-house ceiling in that zip is roughly $950K unless acreage carries it — which makes the silence a pricing answer, not a marketing one.

listings.note: 🔍 LAND DOES NOT PRODUCE SHOWING FORMS, SO THIS CARD MEASURES THE WRONG THING — the real signal is that it out-produces every house here on inbound. ⚠️ Two people are waiting and both answers already exist: the builder off the yard sign is eight days without a callback, and the furthest-along buyer is on day fourteen waiting for the perc answer your teammate already found. 🔴 The seller said “I'll call you back asap” yesterday and never did.

⭐ THIS WEEK IS THE ARGUMENT FOR PRE-BOOKING IT. Willow Point ran ads three days before anyone toured it, then took five bookings and an offer in seven days once the market found it. 🔍 The gap that costs money is between photos-ready and booked — five days wide here, and entirely inside your control.
